Het College bevestigt de ontvangst van een aanvraag om een handelsvergunning of van
                                                een aanvulling daarop als bedoeld in
artikel 4:5 van de Algemene wet bestuursrecht
, schriftelijk binnen een week.
2
Het College neemt binnen 210 dagen na ontvangst van een aanvraag een besluit of een
                                                handelsvergunning wordt verleend. Deze termijn wordt opgeschort gedurende een door
                                                het College gestelde termijn waarbinnen de aanvrager de gelegenheid heeft door het
                                                College verlangde aanvullende gegevens over te leggen.
3
Bij ministeriële regeling worden, met het oog op de volgtijdelijke of de gelijktijdige
                                                verlening van een handelsvergunning voor hetzelfde geneesmiddel in meer dan één lidstaat,
                                                regels gesteld met betrekking tot de door de aanvrager en het College te volgen procedure.
                                                De termijn van 210 dagen, bedoeld in het tweede lid, is niet van toepassing.
4
Indien bij het College een aanvraag om een handelsvergunning is ingediend en het College
                                                constateert dat in een andere lidstaat reeds een aanvraag om een handelsvergunning
                                                voor hetzelfde geneesmiddel in behandeling is, staakt hij de behandeling en deelt
                                                de aanvrager mede dat de procedure, bedoeld in het derde lid, van toepassing is.
5
Indien de aanvraag een geneesmiddel betreft waarvoor in een andere lidstaat reeds
                                                een handelsvergunning is verleend en de aanvraag niet overeenkomstig de procedure,
                                                bedoeld in het derde lid, is ingediend, wijst het College de aanvraag af.
6

translation_review.raw_machine_translation: The College shall acknowledge receipt of an application for a marketing authorisation or an addition thereto referred to in Article 4:5 of the General Administrative Law Act, in writing within one week. 2 The College shall decide whether to grant a marketing authorisation within 210 days of receipt of an application.  This period shall be suspended for a period set by the College within which the applicant has the opportunity to submit additional information requested by the College. 3 Ministerial arrangements shall lay down rules concerning the procedure to be followed by the applicant and the College in order to ensure that the same medicinal product is authorised on a temporary or simultaneous basis in more than one Member State. The period of 210 days referred to in paragraph 2 shall not apply. 4 If an application for a marketing authorisation has been submitted to the College and the College finds that an application for a marketing authorisation for the same medicinal product is already pending in another Member State, it shall cease the treatment and inform the applicant that the procedure referred to in paragraph 3 applies. 5 If the application concerns a medicinal product already authorised in another Member State and the application has not been submitted in accordance with the procedure referred to in paragraph 3, the College shall reject the application. 6
translation_review.checked_translation: The Board shall acknowledge receipt of an application for marketing authorisation or a supplement as referred to in Article 4:5 of the General Administrative Law Act in writing within one week. 2. The Board shall decide within 210 days of receipt whether to grant marketing authorisation. This period is suspended during the period set by the Board for the applicant to submit additional information requested by the Board. 3. Ministerial regulations shall establish the procedure for the applicant and the Board for sequential or simultaneous marketing authorisation of the same medicine in more than one Member State. The 210-day period in paragraph 2 does not apply. 4. If an application is filed with the Board and the Board finds that an application for the same medicine is already under consideration in another Member State, it shall stop processing and inform the applicant that paragraph 3 applies. 5. If the application concerns a medicine already authorised in another Member State and has not been submitted under the procedure in paragraph 3, the Board shall reject it. [Beginning of paragraph 6 outside selected provision.]
translation_review.check_note: Material repair: volgtijdelijke means sequential, not temporary. Checked 210-day exception, clock suspension, must stop processing, and rejection outside the EU procedure.

supplemental_reviewed_clauses.verbatim_extracted_text:
If a medicine is already authorised in an EU country and you want bring it to market in another member state, for example the Netherlands, you follow the
mutual recognition procedure
. This makes your medicine available to the Dutch market by recognition of the assessment by a
Reference Member State
(RMS).
If you want to put a medicine to market for the first time in more EU countries, you follow the
decentralised procedure
.
If you want to put a medicine to market for the first time in all EU countries, you follow the
centralised procedure
.
Medicines for children
have a stricter procedure.
Products that have identical dossiers to previously authorised products can follow a
simplified procedure
.
For the marketing authorisation, you must provide a dossier of the medicine. The medicine is then assessed for safety and efficacy. Which organisation makes the assessment depends on the procedure. For the Dutch market (national procedure), the Dutch Medicines Evaluation Board (MEB) issues the marketing authorisation.
Validity of the marketing authorisation
